clue.text: Request for light haircut is in slightly bad taste

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what you tell a barber who should take only a little hair away
second meaning: somewhat improper or unacceptable, as a remark can be

explanation.walkthrough: The same three-word phrase is a literal instruction at the barber's and an idiom for mild impropriety.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal trimming instruction and an idiom for a remark that is a little improper or out of order.

clue.text: West African spun a fib and fled

indicators.note: spinning a tale suggests twisting it, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ran away, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone from West Africa told a lie and then ran off.
explanation.walkthrough: Biafra was the breakaway state in south-east Nigeria in the late 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biafran is a person from Biafra, a former secessionist region of Nigeria in West Africa.

clue.text: Theatre using those ancient Roman numerals

parts.note: the old means those people who are aged, as in 'the old and the young'
VI and C are both Roman numerals, six and a hundred

explanation.surface: A playhouse making use of the old Roman way of writing numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Vic is a famous theatre in London, near Waterloo station.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Vic is a celebrated London playhouse, so it is an example of a theatre.

clue.text: Said by some to be confused, having weaknesses

indicators.note: only in some accents, those that drop the R, do the two words sound alike, hence 'by some'

parts.note: floored means baffled or confused

explanation.surface: Some people describe someone muddled as being full of failings.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the R is silent, so the word for baffled is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawed has defects or imperfections, so it is having weaknesses.

clue.text: In middle of day poor horse is an unusual shape

indicators.note: the horse is placed in the midday word, so it sits within it

parts.note: noon is the middle of the day
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: A sorry-looking horse at midday forms a strange figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of day' looks like it means the letter A from 'day'; it is the whole time of day, NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a nine-sided polygon, a figure seldom met, so an unusual shape.

clue.text: Preparing to face bowler — out!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket the batter ... is the one about to receive the next ball
second meaning: workers who are out have walked off the job in a dispute

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out!' looks like an umpire's cricket call, but it is the industrial sense of workers having walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket it describes the batter receiving deliveries; in industry it describes workers taking action by stopping work.

clue.text: Some criminal I bill for this defence

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run hidden inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word, the lone I and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A crook offers to charge for this excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere at the time of a crime, used as a legal defence.

clue.text: Start a song where one is in the garden

definitions.text: where one is in the garden

parts.note: to open is to begin or start
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Begin singing a tune while outdoors among the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outside in a garden means being outdoors, under the sky, in the fresh air rather than indoors.

clue.text: Glass to position around a side

parts.note: crystal is fine glass

indicators.note: the word for position goes around the A, enclosing it

parts.note: a place is a position
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to set a glass around one edge of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a team: Crystal Palace is a London football club, named after the vast glass exhibition hall that once stood there.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal Palace is an English professional football team, and a side is a sports team.

clue.text: One may be snapping on the phone

definitions.text: One may be snapping on the phone

parts.note: seems to describe a person speaking curtly, but snapping here means taking photographs
seems to mean during a call, but it means built into the handset

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is someone being short-tempered during a call; the real reading is the device in a mobile that takes snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile phones carry a built-in device for taking photographs, which are informally called snaps.

clue.text: Church having had steeple replaced showed a sign of life

definitions.meaning: first meaning, punning: a church given its spire again has been ...
second meaning: breathed

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful invented word, RE- (again) plus SPIRED (given a spire).
explanation.definitionFit: To respire is to breathe, and breathing is the basic evidence that a creature is alive.

clue.text: A threatening alternative

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the menacing tag ending an ultimatum, as in 'pay up
second meaning: otherwise, introducing another option

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both a plain way of offering another option and the ominous tag on an ultimatum.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means otherwise, offering a second option, and is also the stock close of a menacing ultimatum.

clue.text: Spirit of the theatre?

parts.note: seems to mean an atmosphere or ghost, but it is a kind of antiseptic alcohol named after the hospital trade
seems to mean the stage, but it means the operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the soul of the stage; the answer belongs to the hospital's operating theatre, and surgical spirit is a disinfectant.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical means relating to operations, which take place in an operating theatre; surgical spirit is the antiseptic used there.

clue.text: Rascal that can beat ten?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dishonest rogue
second meaning: the jack, a playing card ranking just above the ten

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is from card games, where the knave (jack) outranks the ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is an old word for a scoundrel and also the jack in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Curious boy tracks what happened before start of film

definitions.text: what happened before start of film

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters are arranged in a strange new order

parts.note: these nine letters are exactly the letters needed, taken as written

explanation.surface: An inquisitive lad follows the trail of events that preceded a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of film' looks like a call for the letter F; it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstory is the history of characters or events leading up to the point where a narrative begins.

clue.text: Review what shoplifter did

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to assess a situation
second meaning, literal: a shoplifter took goods, or stock, from a store

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for pausing to assess is read literally as stealing merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: To take stock is an idiom for pausing to assess one's situation; literally it means removing a shop's merchandise.

clue.text: Witty speech when replanting pear tree

indicators.note: replanting moves the tree, so these letters are set down again in a new order

parts.note: the tree's name, taken as written, supplies all eight letters

explanation.surface: Clever banter while a gardener moves a fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, clever conversational reply and banter.

clue.text: These toadies produce feeling of revulsion

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: the sycophants, since creeps are people who fawn on others
second meaning: a shudder of disgust or unease

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a noun phrase the answer names a set of fawning people; as an idiom it names a shudder of unease.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies are crawlers or creeps, and the idiom 'gives me the creeps' means causes disgust or unease.

clue.text: Keep pulling the sack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sailors' chant urging continued hauling on a rope
second meaning: dismissal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag being hauled; it is dismissal from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Heave-ho is a hauling cry used to encourage effort, and informally means dismissal or rejection.

clue.text: Extremely sick and ailing, get expertise

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: only its first and last letters are kept
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Someone very unwell still gains some proficiency.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill is ability or proficiency gained through practice, which is what expertise means.

clue.text: Right to feed more underweight student

indicators.note: feeding puts something into a mouth, so this letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: leaner means thinner

explanation.surface: It is proper to give extra food to a skinny pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone who is learning, a pupil or student.

clue.text: Group of eight moving to cave

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift position, so these are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, these six letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: Eight people relocating into a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is a set of eight, such as eight lines of a sonnet or eight notes of a scale.

clue.text: Avalanche made by returning crew

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a landslide, a fall of earth
second meaning: a ship's crew makes ... on arriving back at land

explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' looks like a reversal signal; it describes sailors coming back to shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Landfall means a landslide, and also a ship's arrival at land after a voyage.

clue.text: Refuse to be less than modest

indicators.note: the answer is something less than the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: demure means reserved and modest

explanation.surface: Declining to be anything other than humble.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, close to declining or refusing.

clue.text: Careless sort of work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: offhand, unconcerned
second meaning: ... work is irregular, temporary employment

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one adjective, the attitude and the type of job.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual means relaxed or offhand, and casual labour is occasional work without a fixed contract.

clue.text: Such a seal disguising the crime

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so these letters are rearranged to hide them

parts.note: taken as written, these eight letters are the raw material

explanation.surface: A seal that hides the evidence of an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight closure is called a hermetic seal, so the adjective names that kind of seal.

clue.text: Acres certain to be plentiful

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for acre or acres in land measurement
bound means sure or certain, as in 'bound to happen'

explanation.surface: There are enough acres to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to exist in large numbers or great quantity.

clue.text: One attending royalty has no time for messenger

indicators.note: the word for an attendant at court goes without the letter for time

parts.note: a courtier is an attendant at a royal court

explanation.surface: A royal attendant too busy for anything becomes a delivery person.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier carries letters, parcels or messages, so is a messenger.

clue.text: Shortly get money for church in Borders town

indicators.note: said shortly, the word is cut short and loses its last letter

parts.note: to sell something is to get money for it
kirk is the Scottish word for church

explanation.surface: Briefly raising money for a church in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borders is a region of southern Scotland, next to England, which suits the Scottish word for church.
explanation.definitionFit: Selkirk is a historic town in the Scottish Borders region.
